authority: diagnostic: paper only, not investment advice
flags: Wise Group plc completed its dual listing, transferring its primary listing to Nasdaq on May 11, 2026, and became the ultimate parent company of Wise Limited (previously named Wise plc) on May 8, 2026 by means of a Scheme of Arrangement pursuant to Part 26 of the U.K. Companies Act 2006.

business_model.claim: Wise sells through three product offerings: Wise Account for personal customers, Wise Business for small and medium-sized businesses, and Wise Platform for banks, financial institutions and enterprises.
quotes: We market our services through three product offerings: Wise Account for personal customers, Wise Business for small and medium-sized businesses, and Wise Platform for banks, financial institutions and enterprises.

business_model.claim: Wise does not report separate operating segments for Wise Account, Wise Business, and Wise Platform; revenue is reported by the nature of the underlying services provided, which are consistent across all three product offerings.
quotes: We report our revenue based on the nature of the underlying services provided, which are consistent across all three product offerings.

business_model.basis: Stated in 20-F MD&A (P3) and confirmed in the income statement (F2).
business_model.claim: The primary revenue stream is cross-border payment services, including money transfers, currency conversions and account services, which generated $1,893.6 (table in millions) in FY2026.
quotes: revenue from cross-border payment services, including money transfers, currency conversions and account services

business_model.claim: Card revenue, which mainly comprises interchange and other card usage fees, is a secondary revenue stream; card revenue was 16% of net revenue in FY2026.
quotes: card revenue refers to debit card services and mainly comprises interchange and other card usage fees
the proportion of net revenue that is card revenue, which was 16% for the financial year ended March 31, 2026

business_model.claim: Other revenue streams include account top-ups, same-currency transfers, one-time business account setup fees, physical card provision/replacement fees, and Wise Assets management fees.
quotes: other revenue from account top-ups, same-currency transfers, one-time fee charged to Wise business customers, fees earned for the provision or replacement of physical cards and Wise Assets management fees

business_model.basis: Stated in 20-F MD&A (P3) and confirmed in the income statement (F2).
business_model.claim: Interest income on customer balances is a material revenue component, contributing $806.1 (table in millions) in FY2026, earned from holding customer funds as cash or investing them in highly liquid permitted financial assets.
quotes: Interest income on customer balances is earned from holding customer funds as cash and cash equivalents or investing them into highly liquid permitted financial assets.

business_model.claim: Cross-border volume, the total value of transactions where source and target currencies differ, was $243.5 billion in FY2026, up from $185.2 billion in FY2025, and is the primary volume driver of transaction revenue.
quotes: In the financial year ended March 31, 2026, our cross-border volume was $243.5 billion, up from $185.2 billion in the financial year ended March 31, 2025.

business_model.claim: The cross-border take rate (cross-border revenue divided by cross-border volume) declined from 0.58% in FY2025 to 0.52% in FY2026, with personal take rates falling from 0.63% to 0.57% and business take rates from 0.44% to 0.39%, reducing net revenue growth relative to volume growth.
quotes: Our cross-border take rate decreased from an average of 0.58% for the financial year ended March 31, 2025 to 0.52% for the financial year ended March 31, 2026, with personal customer cross-border take rates decreasing from 0.63% to 0.57% and business customer cross-border take rates decreasing from 0.44% to 0.39%.

business_model.claim: Active customers (unique customers completing at least one cross-border transaction) grew from 15.6 million in FY2025 to 18.9 million in FY2026, underpinning volume growth.
quotes: Growth in cross-border volume over these periods was underpinned by growth in active customers, which increased from 15.6 million in the financial year ended March 31, 2025 to 18.9 million in the financial year ended March 31, 2026.

business_model.claim: Cross-border volume in FY2026 split into $173.0 billion personal and $70.5 billion business, up from $135.7 billion and $49.5 billion in FY2025 respectively; Wise Business represented approximately one quarter of transaction activity, while Wise Platform generated less than 10% of overall transaction activity.
quotes: Cross-border volume was split between personal cross-border volume of $173.0 billion and business cross-border volume of $70.5 billion, up from $135.7 billion and $49.5 billion in the financial years ended March 31, 2026 and 2025, respectively.
Wise Platform does not yet generate a material percentage (i.e., it currently generates less than 10%) of the Group's overall transaction activity

business_model.basis: Stated in 20-F income statement (F2) and MD&A (P3).
business_model.claim: Total operating expenses of $1,912.1 (table in millions) in FY2026 grew 39% year-over-year, driven by increases across all five cost lines: transaction expense (36%), technology and development (38%), servicing (38%), marketing and sales (62%), and general and administrative (40%).
quotes: Total operating expenses | (1,912.1) | (1,370.7) | (541.4) | 39%

business_model.basis: Stated in 20-F income statement (F2) and MD&A (P3).
business_model.claim: Transaction expense, the cost of processing and settling transactions and providing debit card services, grew from $378.0 to $513.6 (table in millions), a 36% increase, and is the single largest operating cost line.
quotes: Transaction expense (excluding depreciation and amortization) consists of the costs incurred by Wise in processing and settlement of transactions as well as providing debit card services.

business_model.basis: Stated in 20-F income statement (F2) and MD&A (P3); engineer count from P1.
business_model.claim: Technology and development expenses, covering engineering and product team costs, cloud infrastructure, software subscriptions and AI solutions, grew from $314.1 to $434.3 (table in millions), a 38% increase.
quotes: Technology and development expenses consist of employee-related expenses for our engineering and product teams, including salaries, benefits and share-based compensation expenses, professional services fees and costs for software subscription services dedicated for the use of our technology teams, cloud infrastructure costs as well as costs of other company-wide technology tools, including AI solutions.

business_model.basis: Stated in 20-F MD&A (P3) as a forward-looking statement.

quotes: Cross-border volume was split between personal cross-border volume of $173.0 billion and business cross-border volume of $70.5 billion, up from $135.7 billion and $49.5 billion in the financial years ended March 31, 2026 and 2025, respectively.

competitive_position.claim: Over half of all transactions in the year ended March 31, 2026 were routed through Wise's direct connections to domestic payment systems rather than third-party intermediaries.
quotes: a cross-border transaction where we are directly connected to the relevant domestic payment systems and do not rely on a third party to receive or disburse funds, which represents over half of all transactions processed during the year ended March 31, 2026

competitive_position.claim: Customer holdings across cash and Wise Assets balances equaled $39 billion as of March 31, 2026, including $9.0 billion in assets under custody.
quotes: As of March 31, 2026, our customers' holdings across their cash and Wise Assets balances equaled $39 billion, reflecting the trust we have built with our customers. This included $9.0 billion held with Wise Assets (i.e. assets under custody)

competitive_position.claim: Wise's cross-border take rate declined from 0.58% to 0.52% year-over-year, with personal rates falling from 0.63% to 0.57% and business rates from 0.44% to 0.39%, as a deliberate pricing strategy to drive volume growth.
quotes: Our cross-border take rate decreased from an average of 0.58% for the financial year ended March 31, 2025 to 0.52% for the financial year ended March 31, 2026, with personal customer cross-border take rates decreasing from 0.63% to 0.57% and business customer cross-border take rates decreasing from 0.44% to 0.39%.

competitive_position.basis: Stated as a company estimate in P1 (Item 4 of the 20-F).
competitive_position.claim: Wise's total addressable market is estimated at $43 trillion in annual cross-border payments, with the company's $243.5 billion volume representing a small fraction of that market.
quotes: We estimate that the market for cross-border transactions adds up to $43 trillion worth of cross-border payments every year, and continues to grow.
In other words, the $243.5 billion we moved across borders in the year ended March 31, 2026 is only a fraction of our total addressable market.

competitive_position.claim: Wise's stated long-term aim is for Wise Platform to account for more than 50% of cross-border volume, though it currently generates less than 10% of overall transaction activity.
quotes: Our long-term aim is for Wise Platform to account for more than 50% of Wise's cross-border volume.
Wise Platform does not yet generate a material percentage (i.e., it currently generates less than 10%) of the Group's overall transaction activity

growth_thesis.basis: Stated in P3 narrative and F2 income statement.
growth_thesis.claim: Cross-border volume is the primary growth driver, having grown from $185.2 billion to $243.5 billion in the fiscal year ended March 31, 2026, and transaction revenue is generated as a percentage fee on that volume.
quotes: In the financial year ended March 31, 2026, our cross-border volume was $243.5 billion, up from $185.2 billion in the financial year ended March 31, 2025.
Cross-border take rate is calculated as cross-border revenue divided by cross-border volume.

growth_thesis.basis: Stated in P3 Key Operating Metrics section.
growth_thesis.claim: Active customer acquisition is the key volume driver: active customers grew from 15.6 million to 18.9 million, with personal customers rising from 14.9 million to 18.0 million and business customers from 0.7 million to 0.9 million.
quotes: active customers, which increased from 15.6 million in the financial year ended March 31, 2025 to 18.9 million in the financial year ended March 31, 2026. This was split between active personal customers, which grew from 14.9 million to 18.0 million, and active business customers which grew from 0.7 million to 0.9 million.

growth_thesis.basis: Stated in P3; the company explicitly links take-rate cuts to volume and customer growth.
growth_thesis.claim: Deliberate take-rate reduction is a growth lever: the cross-border take rate fell from 0.58% to 0.52%, with personal rates dropping from 0.63% to 0.57% and business rates from 0.44% to 0.39%, to make products more attractive and drive volume.
quotes: Our cross-border take rate decreased from an average of 0.58% for the financial year ended March 31, 2025 to 0.52% for the financial year ended March 31, 2026, with personal customer cross-border take rates decreasing from 0.63% to 0.57% and business customer cross-border take rates decreasing from 0.44% to 0.39%.

growth_thesis.basis: Stated in P1, P3, and F2 income statement.
growth_thesis.claim: Customer balance growth drives interest income: customer holdings reached $39 billion as of March 31, 2026, generating $806.1 (table in millions) of interest income on customer balances, and personal customer balances grew 38% to $18.8 billion.
quotes: As of March 31, 2026, our customers' holdings across their cash and Wise Assets balances equaled $39 billion, reflecting the trust we have built with our customers.
Personal customer balances also grew significantly, up 38% to $18.8 billion at March 31, 2026 compared to March 31, 2025.

growth_thesis.basis: Stated in P3 business overview and key operating metrics.
growth_thesis.claim: Wise Business is a high-growth segment: it served 850 thousand active business customers, business cross-border volumes grew 42% to $70.5 billion, and business deposits grew from $8.4 billion to $11.2 billion.
quotes: Wise Business had 850 thousand active business customers, including an average of 29 thousand new businesses joining per month during this period.
Business customer deposits held totaled $11.2 billion at March 31, 2026 as compared to $8.4 billion at March 31, 2025.

growth_thesis.basis: Stated as a strategic aim in P3; current contribution is quantified as less than 10%.
growth_thesis.claim: Wise Platform is the stated long-term growth engine, currently generating less than 10% of overall transaction activity, with the long-term aim of accounting for more than 50% of Wise's cross-border volume.
quotes: Wise Platform does not yet generate a material percentage (i.e., it currently generates less than 10%) of the Group's overall transaction activity and as such is included within both Wise Account and Wise Business activity.
Our long-term aim is for Wise Platform to account for more than 50% of Wise's cross-border volume.

growth_thesis.basis: Stated in P1 regulatory licenses section; risk noted in P2.
growth_thesis.claim: Regulatory and geographic expansion enables growth: as of March 31, 2026, Wise held over 80 regulatory licenses globally, supporting operations in 40 currencies across 160 countries and territories.
quotes: As of March 31, 2026, we held over 80 regulatory licenses globally, enabling us to offer customers the ability to hold money in 40 currencies and use the Wise Multi-Currency Card (the "Wise Card") to make payments online and in stores in over 40 currencies across 160 countries and territories, and withdraw money from three million ATMs worldwide.

growth_thesis.basis: Stated in P1 technology section; expense growth from F2.
growth_thesis.claim: Technology infrastructure underpins scale and efficiency: over 1,000 engineers process over 4.7 million transactions a day on a single global technology stack, with over half of transactions routed through direct connections to domestic payment systems.
quotes: As of March 31, 2026, over 1,000 engineers across four continents work to evolve and deploy our technology, which processes over 4.7 million transactions a day, including weekends.
This speed is driven in part by routing over half of all transactions in the period through our connections to domestic payment systems.

growth_thesis.basis: Stated as company estimates in P1; not independently verified in the evidence.
growth_thesis.claim: The total addressable market for cross-border payments is estimated at $43 trillion annually, with potential to reach $55 trillion by 2029, meaning Wise's $243.5 billion in FY2026 volume represents a small fraction of the opportunity.
quotes: We estimate that the market for cross-border transactions adds up to $43 trillion worth of cross-border payments every year, and continues to grow.
In other words, the $243.5 billion we moved across borders in the year ended March 31, 2026 is only a fraction of our total addressable market.

growth_thesis.basis: Stated in P1 business overview and P3 revenue description.
growth_thesis.claim: Wise Assets is an emerging growth and retention driver: $9.0 billion in assets under custody as of March 31, 2026, offering customers a return on idle balances while keeping funds accessible.
quotes: This included $9.0 billion held with Wise Assets (i.e. assets under custody), an account feature that helps our customers earn a return on their money while ensuring it remains conveniently accessible.

growth_thesis.basis: Stated in P3 Key Trends section; interest income and expense figures from F2.
growth_thesis.claim: For interest income to continue growing, market interest rates must remain at levels that generate meaningful yield on the $39 billion customer balance base, and Wise must be able to pass a portion of that yield to customers to maintain product attractiveness.
quotes: Interest income on customer balances is affected by the amount of customer deposits we hold and market interest rates.
While our interest framework has historically aimed to ultimately return to our customers 80% of interest income yield greater than 1%, we have not been able to do so across all jurisdictions.

growth_thesis.basis: Stated in F2 income statement and P3 results discussion; the company explicitly attributes the decline to take-rate reduction and increased investment.
growth_thesis.claim: Profitability is currently contracting despite revenue growth: operating income fell 19% to $590.7 (table in millions) and net income declined from $550.3 to $498.7 (table in millions), as total operating expenses grew 39% to $1,912.1 (table in millions) against 19% net revenue growth.
quotes: Our net income was $498.7 million for the financial year ended March 31, 2026, a decline of $51.6 million over the financial year ended March 31, 2025, primarily driven by the reduction in our average cross-border take rate by 0.06 percentage points, from 0.58% to 0.52%, reducing net revenue growth compared to volume growth.

In connection with the completion of our listing on Nasdaq on May 11, 2026, Wise Group plc became the ultimate parent company of Wise Limited (previously named Wise plc) and its consolidated subsidiaries on May 8, 2026 by means of a Scheme of Arrangement pursuant to Part 26 of the U.K. Companies Act 2006.
